## Education

**B.S in Business Economics**

**Minor in Cognitive Science, *w/ a focus on Data Analysis***

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Courses

Here is a table of some of my favorite and most relevant courses to date:\

| Course Title | Description |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Customer Analytics – MGT100 | Applied R to perform customer segmentation, demand estimation, conjoint analysis, and pricing optimization using real business datasets to support data-driven marketing decisions. |
| Detecting Discrimination in Data – ECON185 | Used econometric methods including regression decomposition, difference-in-differences, and instrumental variables to identify and quantify racial and economic disparities in labor markets, policing, and the criminal legal system. |
| Data Science in Practice – COGS108 | Completed a full end-to-end data science project in Python covering data wrangling, EDA, machine learning, NLP, and statistical inference, with emphasis on real-world application and reproducibility. |
| Principles of Data Science – DSC10 | Applied Python programming to explore datasets, draw statistical inferences, and build predictive models using real-world data across multiple disciplines. |
| Data Analytics for Social Sciences – ECON5 | Analyzed real-world social science questions using Excel, Stata, and R, covering data wrangling, regression analysis, and data visualization applied to topics like intergenerational mobility and labor market discrimination. |
| Quantitative Methods in Business – MGT3 | Applied statistical techniques including probability, simulation, Bayesian statistics, forecasting, and optimization to business decision-making problems using R. |
| Experiments in Firms – MGT160 | Designed and ran randomized controlled experiments to test business and policy interventions, applying behavioral economics insights to real organizational questions. |
| Data Visualization – STAT80B | Developed effective data visualizations and infographics using Tableau and Inkscape, applying principles of visual design to communicate complex data clearly and accurately. |
| Beginning Programming in Python – CSE20 | Built foundational Python programming skills including data structures, functions, classes, and file handling through weekly coding assignments. |
| Econometrics A – ECON120A | Built foundational probability and statistical theory for economics, covering sampling distributions, statistical inference, and data analysis using spreadsheets. |
| Econometrics B – ECON120B | Applied core econometric methods including linear regression, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and causal inference techniques to real economic data. |
| Operating Successful Business – MGT71 | Applied operations management frameworks including process analysis, capacity planning, inventory theory, quality management, and lean operations to real-world business strategy. |
| Business Finance – MGT180 | Applied core financial concepts including cash flow valuation, risk analysis, capital budgeting, and stock and bond pricing to real-world corporate and investment decisions using Excel. |
| Product Marketing & Management – MGT103 | Developed skills in market segmentation, customer targeting, product positioning, pricing strategy, and promotion to drive data-informed marketing decisions across the product lifecycle. |
| Microeconomics A – ECON100A | Applied calculus-based optimization to model consumer behavior, including utility maximization, demand functions, labor supply, and decision-making under risk and uncertainty. |
| Microeconomics B – ECON100B | Extended microeconomic theory to analyze market imperfections including monopoly pricing, game theory, oligopoly, externalities, public goods, and asymmetric information. |
| Short Run Macroeconomics – ECON110B | Analyzed the causes of economic recessions, inflation, and business cycles, and evaluated monetary and fiscal policy responses. |
| Managing Diverse Teams – MGT18 | Examined how diversity, social identity, unconscious bias, and cultural intelligence shape team dynamics, and developed practical leadership skills for building inclusive and high-performing workplace teams. |
| Negotiations – MGT162R | Developed analytical and practical negotiation skills through weekly live negotiation exercises, applying frameworks for value claiming, value creation, and multi-party coalition dynamics. |
| Business and Organizational Leadership – MGT164 | Examined key leadership frameworks including power, influence, organizational culture, emotional intelligence, and change management, with weekly written reflections connecting theory to personal leadership development. |
| Calculus III – MATH10C | Extended calculus to multivariable settings, covering vector geometry, partial derivatives, velocity and acceleration vectors, and multivariable optimization problems. |
| Calculus I – MATH11A | Built foundational differential calculus skills including limits, derivatives, and their applications, serving as a prerequisite for upper-division quantitative coursework. |
| Calculus II – MATH11B | Extended integral calculus covering techniques of integration and their applications to real-world problems. |
